next_wave_cards.objective: Implement geoai_completion_inbox_delta(topic, since_cursor, limit) exactly per B277 section_2b/section_2 (deterministic event_id, caller-owned cursor_token format, 5-kind event envelope). Pure function over existing completion_inbox.build_completion_inbox() + core.collision_guard() + core.usage_report() outputs -- no new mutation, no cursor persisted server-side.
acceptance: New tool registered additively in server.py; all 24 existing tools still present (list_tools count check)
event_id is deterministic (same underlying state -> same event_id across two calls)
cursor round-trip: passing back next_cursor from call N returns 0 already-seen events on call N+1 given no new state change
all 5 event_kinds (completion, failure, stale, usage, duplicate_runner) reachable via fixture-injected task states
authority_flags on every event and top-level are all false
no write to task_queue_v1.sqlite; DB fingerprint unchanged before/after

next_wave_cards.objective: Decide and implement WHERE Codex's own orchestration loop persists since_cursor between iterations (session-local state file vs a small dedicated JSON under tools/geoai-task-mcp/data/ vs in-memory only for a single continuous session). This is a Codex-authority decision (cursor consumer identity, retention policy, multi-session semantics) that a worker cannot make unilaterally per B277 section_2b (cursor is caller-owned, not server-owned).
acceptance: Documented cursor storage location and retention policy
Wired into Codex's existing auto-pickup-equivalent loop cadence
No change to geoai_completion_inbox_delta's stateless contract

blockers: OWNER_DELIVERY_CHANNEL_UNDECIDED: no email/Slack/desktop-notify target exists or is chosen; wiring one requires owner-approved external credentials/infra that this task has no authority to select. Cannot be closed by a worker task card alone -- needs an explicit owner decision on channel + credential storage before any implementation task is scoped.

NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ_STILL_OPEN: the B277 event taxonomy is metadata-only (task-card fields); reading and summarizing the actual JSON/JSONL artifact bodies a worker produced is explicitly out of scope for this spec and unaddressed by any next_wave card here -- would need its own read-policy/size-budget design (artifacts can exceed the 25MB single-file budget in aggregate across many tasks).

TRUE_PUSH_MECHANISM_NOT_DESIGNED: this spec only covers an agent-loop-driven automatic pull (section_3); a real push (inotify on task_queue_v1.sqlite, a DB trigger, or a message queue) was explicitly NOT designed here and would be a separate, larger architecture task with its own risk review (write-path changes to a shared, concurrently-written SQLite file).
